rationale_summary: Innovation enablement is the dominant frame because the page justifies AI Act standardisation primarily as a way to provide legal certainty, simplify compliance, lower compliance costs for businesses of all sizes, avoid regulatory fragmentation and redundant compliance efforts, and foster trust and market acceptance through voluntary technical standards and rollout support tools. Economic competitiveness is a close runner-up, reflected in repeated emphasis on European harmonised standards becoming de facto global benchmarks, helping developers compete on a global scale, and positioning the EU to lead globally; innovation enablement edges it out because the operational focus throughout the page is reducing compliance friction and enabling trustworthy adoption rather than zero-sum economic rivalry. Consumer and public safety and fundamental rights appear as secondary background rationales describing the underlying high-risk AI Act objectives (protecting safety, health, and fundamental rights, and meeting high safety standards).
